name: Lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (PSMA-617) - PSMA-positive mCRPC

biomarkers.PSMA: PSMA-positive on PSMA-PET/CT (e.g., Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat PSMA, or F-18 PSMA); not recommended if dominant PSMA-negative lesions are present
biomarkers.note: Lu-177-PSMA-617 targets prostate-specific membrane antigen and requires PSMA-positive disease on PSMA-PET. It is not recommended in patients with dominant PSMA-negative lesions (bone with soft-tissue components >= 1.0 cm, lymph nodes >= 2.5 cm short axis, or solid-organ metastases >= 1.0 cm that lack PSMA uptake). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer, PROS-J (Lu-177-PSMA-617) and Principles of Imaging (PROS-E).

lineOfTherapy: PSMA-directed radioligand therapy for PSMA-positive mCRPC previously treated with an ARPI and taxane-based chemotherapy (category 1; VISION), or considered appropriate to delay chemotherapy after prior ARPI (PSMAfore)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: PSMA-positive disease on PSMA-PET without dominant PSMA-negative lesions
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-J (Lu-177-PSMA-617), prostate lines 3843 to 3849 (PSMA-positive; not recommended with dominant PSMA-negative lesions; PSMA-negative lesion definitions)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: prior ARPI therapy and prior taxane-based chemotherapy, or considered appropriate to delay chemotherapy
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-J, prostate lines 3845 to 3847 (approved for mCRPC treated with ARPI and prior taxane, or appropriate to delay chemotherapy)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: ongoing ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL

exclusionCriteria.requirement: dominant PSMA-negative lesions (metastatic disease lacking PSMA uptake: bone with soft-tissue component >= 1.0 cm, lymph nodes >= 2.5 cm short axis, or solid-organ metastases >= 1.0 cm)

drugs.name: Lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (PSMA-617)

provenance.locator: PROS-J, prostate line 3851 (Lu-177-PSMA-617 is typically administered IV 200 mCi (7.4 GBq) every 6 weeks for up to 6 treatments); Discussion, prostate line 7813 (7.4 GBq or 200 mCi every 6 weeks for 4 to 6)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026, PROS-J (prostate line 3851) and Discussion (prostate line 7813). DOSE: 200 mCi (7.4 GBq) IV every 6 weeks for up to 6 treatments (VISION). UNIT NOTE: the true unit is radioactivity; unit is recorded as mCi (200 mCi = 7.4 GBq), consistent with the schema enum; the dose is source-established, so no field is set to VERIFY. Radioligand: no ISMP tall-man form. Administer by an appropriately licensed facility with gamma-radiation-safety precautions; post-treatment SPECT/PET can be used to monitor PSMA expression for adaptive dosing (PROS-J, prostate line 3852).

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Provide per emetogenic-risk tier around each dose.

supportiveCare: continue ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (PROS-G).
confirm PSMA-positive disease on PSMA-PET before treatment; an FDG PET/CT may help identify low-PSMA / non-PSMA-avid disease that derives less benefit (PROS-J, prostate line 3850).
administer by an appropriately licensed nuclear-medicine facility; treatment rooms monitored for contamination; provide written radiation-safety instructions (PROS-J, prostate lines 3853 to 3855).
cycles: up to 6 treatments (source-stated up to 6; some patients receive 4 to 6).

monitoring: CBC (myelosuppression) before each dose and on follow-up
PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)
PSMA-PET / post-treatment SPECT response and PSMA expression

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 hematologic, renal, or hepatic toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold, dose-reduce, or discontinue per labeling and radiation-safety protocol; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Lu-177-PSMA-617 (VISION) improves overall survival in PSMA-positive mCRPC after ARPI and taxane therapy

guideline.locator: PROS-J (Radiopharmaceutical Therapy, Lu-177-PSMA-617): PSMA-positive requirement and PSMA-negative lesion definitions (prostate lines 3843 to 3849); prior ARPI + taxane or appropriate to delay chemotherapy (prostate lines 3845 to 3847); dose 200 mCi (7.4 GBq) every 6 weeks for up to 6 treatments (prostate line 3851); Discussion 7.4 GBq/200 mCi every 6 weeks for 4 to 6 (prostate line 7813); PROS-E (Principles of Imaging, PSMA-PET)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (PSMA-617) in PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (disease #54 mCRPC; VISION). The radioligand dose (200 mCi / 7.4 GBq IV every 6 weeks for up to 6 treatments) is dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 PROS-J (prostate line 3851) and Discussion (prostate line 7813); the unit is recorded as mCi (200 mCi = 7.4 GBq), so no field is set to VERIFY. Biomarker gate: PSMA-positive disease on PSMA-PET (Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat, or F-18 PSMA), with dominant PSMA-negative lesions as an exclusion (PROS-J). Prior ARPI and taxane therapy, or appropriateness to delay chemotherapy, is required. cycleLengthDays 42 (every 6 weeks) and cycles 6 are source-stated. Ongoing ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL is required. No dose was invented or inferred. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
